To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MDCK–C1 cells have a Na+-independent proton pump and a Na+/H+-exchanger on their apical membrane.

MDCK–C1 cells have a Na+-independent H+-ATPases on their apical membrane, a concanamycinesensitive H+-ATPASE on the apical membrane and basolateral membrane, and a K+- dependent, Schering  28080-sensitive H+–K+-ATPases only on the apical side.
MDCK–C1 cells secrete H+ via a Na+/H+-exchanger and an H+-ATP-ase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms involved in the regulation of intracellular pH (and volume) in MDCK cells.
the characterization of the proton secretion mechanisms of MDCK– C11 cells, a recently cloned cell line that has been shown to be useful in studies of the transport of organic anions.
the mechanisms of intracellular proton secretion, and the role of the vacuole in the regulation of intracellular pH.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MDCK–C1l cells express a Na+/H+, a K+-dependent H+-K+- and a vacuolar H+ ATPase.
the apical membrane of MDCK– C11 cells has a H+-K+- ATPase, a Na+/H+-exchanger and a vacuolar H+ ATPase, while the basolateral membrane has only the last two.
MDCK–C1 cells have Na+/H+ and H+/K+ antiporters, as well as a vacuolar H+ ATPase in their apical membranes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MDCK–C1 cells express a H+-K+- ATPase on their apicale membrane, and a vacuolar-type H+-ATPases on both apical and baso lateral membranes.
MDCK–C1 cells have a basolateral Na+/H+ exchange and a basolateral vacuolar-type H+-ATPases.
the MDCK–C1 and MDCK–C7 cells are the most similar to each other, while the MDCK–A6 and MDCK–A1 cells are the most different.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a novel cell line that has all the characteristics of a good model for the study of ion transport in epithelial cells.

the Na+-independant proton secretion in MD-CK-C11 cells is due to the presence of H+-ATPases on both sides of the cells, and that these H+-ATPasses have different sensitivities to the inhibitors concanamycin and Schering 280.
the apical membrane of MDCK– C11 cells contains a K+-dependent H+-K+-transporting ATPase.
